strengths: The paper addresses an important NLP accessibility problem through compact models for ten Indian languages, including underserved languages such as Konkani, Maithili, and Assamese. The emphasis on CPU deployment has practical value.

Evaluation includes established multilingual benchmarks and comparisons with BLOOM, BLOOMZ, Sarvam, OpenHathi, and Airavata. Reported instruction-tuning improvements are promising; for example, Bangla Belebele accuracy increases from 25.11 to 32.45.

Culturally grounded data curation, including 5,000 manually created Bangla instructions, and native-speaker evaluation are appropriate directions. The extensive generation examples permit some inspection of model behavior.
weaknesses: The central RoPE memory-efficiency claim is unsupported and lacks a convincing mechanism. Rescaling positional embeddings alone does not reduce the token activations or attention memory required to process a longer sequence. The paper provides neither a precise algorithm nor controlled memory measurements or context-length ablations. Training these small models with a 1,024-token context on a 40GB A100 does not establish the claimed architectural advance.

Reproducibility is substantially inadequate. Architecture configurations, vocabulary sizes, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, batch sizes, training steps, and fine-tuning settings are missing. Corpus sources, unique corpus sizes, language/domain proportions, and split construction are insufficiently specified. No release location is supplied for the models, tokenizers, datasets, or implementation. Reported token totals and broad preprocessing descriptions cannot substitute for these details.

The human evaluation cannot support broad claims of superiority over larger LLMs. It uses only four prompts per evaluated language, generally with three generations each, without reporting rater allocation, blinding, agreement, uncertainty, or a sufficiently detailed rubric. Assigning factuality zero when a claim cannot be verified conflates unverifiability with falsehood. The October 2023 ChatGPT web comparisons also lack a reproducible, matched generation protocol. Many other generation baselines predominantly target English, limiting what their failures establish.

The claimed low-resource-to-high-resource transfer is not demonstrated by the benchmark evidence. For example, mParamanu obtains 24.84 on Hindi MMLU and 33.70 on Hindi XNLI, approximately their respective chance levels of 25 and 33.3. Small differences among such scores, without uncertainty estimates, cannot establish effective transfer. Controlled comparisons are needed to isolate script grouping and corpus balancing from differences in model capacity, tokenization, and training data.

The tokenizer contribution is insufficiently specified and validated. Figure 3 does not explain how BPE and Unigram models are combined or how vocabulary intersections preserve coverage. Figure 2 imports baseline fertility scores without establishing a common evaluation corpus and vocabulary-budget protocol. Moreover, Table 3 compares per-token perplexities across languages and tokenizers; these values are not directly comparable and cannot establish tokenizer superiority or relative undertraining. A common normalization, such as bits per byte, and downstream ablations are needed.

The efficiency evaluation lacks essential controls. Table 18 omits CPU specifications, thread counts, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and implementation details, and includes no matched baseline measurements. Parameter counts support compactness, but the reported timings do not isolate benefits from the proposed tokenizer or architecture.

Reporting inconsistencies materially weaken confidence. Section 4.3 and Section 5 describe 23,000 instruction examples, whereas the benchmark discussion specifies 27,000 and, for Hindi, an additional 52,000 Alpaca examples. In Table 7, the six Hindi-instruct scores average 38.49, not the reported 40.14. These require an audit of dataset versions, checkpoint identities, and result calculations. Together with the methodological gaps, substantial new validation and documentation are necessary before the contribution meets Findings standards, supporting resubmission after the next cycle.
